content.text:
Silhouette: Horizontal red fox frame carried on two hind legs, barn owl wings in place of the forelegs. Host frame: the red fox sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a red fox and a barn owl. Head of the red fox, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: red fox body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the barn owl, as parts and materials on the red fox's own body: broad wings of layered flight feathers in place of the forelegs, standing on two hind legs; wings sized for flight; deep keel and heavy flight chest. Coat texture and patches follow the body outline. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature silhouette**
I'm planning a single creature with a red fox body and head on two hind legs, swapping the forelegs for broad barn owl wings of layered flight feathers, keeping dense fur, a plain coat, and a clear, uncluttered face with visible eyes.
**Drafting natural history illustration**
I'm preparing a scientific-style drawing of the hybrid: fox head with red fur, barn-owl wings as forelimbs, standing on two hind legs with a deep keel and heavy flight chest, side three-quarter view on a plain light background with natural lighting and soft shadow.
